history.period: 11th century CE (temple structure); idol traditionally dated older
history.summary: CONFLICT (verify): sources disagree on antiquity. Travel and news sources say the temple at Hathiagarh in Tewar village, on the Bhedaghat road about 13 km from Jabalpur, was built in the 11th century by Kalachuri king Karnadeva (Lakshmikarna), with an inscription on site confirming this; the temple was the kuldevi shrine of the Kalachuri kings. Other local accounts claim a 7th-century (1400-year-old) foundation, and legend holds the goddess's presence dates to the Dwapara era with Karna of the Mahabharata as her devotee. The goddess's idol is traditionally said to have emerged from the ground. The shrine is regarded as a tantra centre of the Shakti tradition. CSV town 'Jabalpur' corrected: the temple is in Tewar village (the ancient city of Tripuri, Kalachuri capital 8th-13th c.), not Jabalpur city. Coordinates are approximate (place-listing data, verify).

name: Tripur Sundari Mandir
town_description: Tewar is a village in Jabalpur district, Madhya Pradesh, about 13 km from Jabalpur on the Bhedaghat road. It is the site of Tripuri, an ancient city-state and the capital of the later Kalachuris from the 8th to 13th centuries, celebrated in inscriptions and Sanskrit literature under names including Tripura and Tiura.
